intro: The present perfect connects a past event or period with the present. Its use varies by region.
p.he.consejo: The h is silent: say «e». It always goes next to the participle: «he vivido».
p.has.consejo: It is said «as». It is not the verb «hacer»: here «has» helps the participle.
p.ha.consejo: No accent and with h: «ha». The preposition «a» has no h: «voy a casa».
p.hemos.consejo: For nosotros: «hemos vivido». For vosotros you say «habéis vivido», mainly in Spain.
p.han.consejo: It also serves for ustedes: «ustedes han visto». It is the plural form most used in America.
p.vivido.consejo: Verbs in -er and -ir form the participle with -ido: comer, comido; vivir, vivido.
p.estado.consejo: It is used to say where you have been: «he estado en Perú». It ends in -ado, like -ar verbs.
p.visto.consejo: Ver is irregular: the participle is «visto», not «vido». It is written with v.
p.hecho.consejo: Hacer is irregular: «hecho». The initial h is silent and ch sounds like in «chocolate».
p.escrito.consejo: Escribir is irregular: «escrito», not «escribido». It also works as an adjective: «un texto escrito».
p.dicho.consejo: Decir is irregular: «dicho». «He dicho la verdad». It is written with ch.
p.ya.consejo: It usually goes before the verb: «ya he comido». It means the event has already happened.
p.todavía no.consejo: It goes before «he»: «todavía no he comido». The accent is on the i.
p.aún no.consejo: It means the same as «todavía no». With an accent on the u: «aún».
b1.texto:
The present perfect is formed with **he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han** + **participle**. **Habéis** is used with vosotros, mainly in Spain; with ustedes use **han**.

- **He vivido** aquí dos años y todavía vivo aquí. (The period continues now.)
- ¿**Has estado** en México?

Regular participles: **hablado, comido, vivido**. Very common irregulars: **visto, hecho, escrito, abierto, dicho, puesto**.

**Ya** means something happened before now. **Todavía no** and **aún no** mean it has not happened yet.

In much of Spain it is used for events in a time that includes today: **hoy he visto** a friend. In many parts of America the indefinido is preferred in these cases. It changes by region.
b2.f2.texto: I haven't made that trip yet.
b2.f3.texto: I have lived there for two years.
b2.f5.texto: I have made three good friends.
b2.f6.texto: I haven't written the trip plan yet.
b2.f7.texto: My friend has said that the trip is lovely.
b4.texto:
A recipe with two ingredients:

- **Haber** in the present: **he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han**.
- **Participle**: **-ar → -ado** (hablado) and **-er / -ir → -ido** (comido, vivido).
- Irregulars: **ver → visto**, **hacer → hecho**, **escribir → escrito**, **abrir → abierto**, **decir → dicho**, **poner → puesto**.

The participle **does not change** with haber: **he visto**, **hemos visto**. Nothing goes between **haber** and the participle: **ya he visto**, never «he ya visto». Pronouns go before: **lo he visto**.

**Ya** goes before the verb: **ya he comido**. **Todavía no** and **aún no** too: **todavía no he comido**.
b4.e0.texto: We have eaten at home today.
b4.e1.texto: My parents have opened the window.
b5.f0.texto: I have lived many years in this house by the river.
b5.f1.texto: The mist has covered the water every morning.
b5.f2.texto: The bells have woken the village with a soft sound.
b5.f3.texto: My neighbours have opened the windows to the first sun.
b5.f4.texto: I have seen the same golden light on the roof every day.
b5.f5.texto: This morning I have written a long letter to my grandmother.
b5.f6.texto: The white paper has kept the smell of coffee.
b5.f7.texto: My hand has drawn each letter with great care.
b5.f8.texto: I have not closed the blue envelope yet.
b5.f9.texto: The light from the courtyard has slowly come in through the open window.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! Ver is irregular and its participle is «visto».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Vido» does not exist: the participle of ver is irregular.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Veído» looks regular, but ver does not use it: it is «visto».
b6.pregunta: What is the participle of ver?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «He» is only for yo. My friend is él.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Hemos» is for nosotros, not for a single person.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Well done: él, ella and usted use «ha».
b7.pregunta: Which form of haber goes with «mi amigo»?
b8.traduccion: I have lived here for two years
b9.o0.refuerzo: It looks regular, but hacer has an irregular participle.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Correct: «he hecho», with an initial h and ch.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Hice» is the indefinido of yo, not a participle.
b9.pregunta: What is the participle of hacer?
b10.o0.refuerzo: That regular form does not exist: escribir is irregular.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Well done! Escribir gives «escrito» in the perfect.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Escribí» is indefinido and does not go after «he».
b10.pregunta: Which participle of escribir completes the sentence?
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «ya» says the event happened before now.
p.comido.consejo: With «haber», the past participle of «comer» is «comido»: «he comido».
p.campanas.consejo: The stress falls on PA, the middle syllable.
p.guardado.consejo: The u is sounded: «guardar» begins like «guerra».
p.dibujado.consejo: It ends in -ado, like other verbs ending in -ar.
p.entrado.consejo: «Entrar» means to go in, so its participle is «entrado».
